- Thrombo-embolic END in 76% (mostly artery-to-artery embolism from thrombus fragmentation), associated with new intracranial occlusion (76% vs 0%, p<0.001, table 2).

- Small sample size (n=74)

- Some patients with baseline severe carotid stenosis may have been misclassified as iICAo

- No control group (non-IVT)

On multiphase CTA, you compare the affected side to the unaffected side for extent and prominence of pial arterial filling across phases, producing a score from 0 to 5:
• 0: No visible collaterals (no/minimal pial filling in the occluded territory).
• 1: Collaterals fill ≤ 50% of the territory.
• 2: Collaterals fill > 50% but < 100% of the territory.
• 3: 100% filling, but less than the contralateral side (delayed and or less prominent).
• 4: 100% filling equal to the contralateral side.
• 5: 100% filling greater than the contralateral side (very robust collaterals).

7.2. Implications:
• IVT may speed up distal intracranial embolism from ICA thrombus fragmentation in minor stroke with iICAo, leading to earlier but not more frequent END. 
  • Benefit/risk ratio of IVT may not favor its use in nondisabling symptoms.
  • Close monitoring in endovascular-capable center warranted regardless of treatment. 
  • Other therapeutic options to consider: early post-IVT antiplatelet, anticoagulation, direct EVT
7.3. Limitations:
• Observational study, confounding by indication possible (IVT patients had higher NIHSS, earlier admission)
  • Moderate sample size constraining statistical analysis
  • Large inclusion period (2006–2020) with potential clinical management changes
  • Variable antithrombotic regimens in non-IVT group
  • No direct EVT comparison group
  • Cannot generalize to more severe iICAo presentations.

7.1. Key findings:
• END occurred in 19.1% (207/1,083) of minor stroke patients with anterior LVO, 85% of patients developed END within 48 h of the LKW time
  • Hypertension, higher baseline NIHSS, extracranial ICA occlusion, and tandem lesions independently predicted END
  • EVT did not improve 90-day functional outcome (mRS 0–1  PS-matched OR 0.99 [0.63–1.54]) and increased hemorrhage risk (significant hemorrhage PS-matched OR 4.51 [1.59–12.80], any hemorrhage PS-matched OR 3.17 [95% CI, 1.76–5.69])
  • EVT showed no benefit regardless of whether END occurred before EVT or not
7.2. Implications:
• EVT may not be beneficial for mild LVO patients (NIHSS <6) and may increase hemorrhage risk
  • Extracranial ICA and tandem lesions might help identify patients at higher risk for END
  • Results support a conservative initial approach with close monitoring rather than routine EVT in minor stroke with LVO
7.3. Limitations:
• East Asian population (higher prevalence of intracranial stenosis, may limit generalizability)
  • Observational registry study (no randomization)
  • Variable imaging protocols and treatment decisions across 16 centers
